question.body:
Consider $dif y / dif x = -x y^2 / 2$. Let $y=f(x)$ satisfy $f(-1)=2$.

(a) On the provided axes, sketch the slope field at the twelve indicated points.

#image("/imgs/ap-calc-ab-2005-form-b-frq-06-prompt-b6553edd-3e90-4eeb-8d43-7d799208e18b-1_595_808_1169_660.jpg", width: 70%)

(b) Write the equation of the line tangent to $f$ at $x=-1$.

(c) Find $f(x)$.
question.solution:
(a) Horizontal segments occur where $x=0$ or $y=0$. At the remaining marked points, use slope $-x y^2/2$.

(b) At $(-1,2)$,
$ f'(-1) = -(-1)(2)^2 / 2 = 2. $
Thus the tangent line is $y - 2 = 2(x + 1)$.

(c) Separate variables:
$ 1/y^2 dif y = -x/2 dif x. $
Integrating gives $-1/y = -x^2/4 + C$. Using $f(-1)=2$ gives $C=-1/4$, so
$ f(x) = frac(4, x^2 + 1). $
